## Before you start

- **Designed for:** learners with little or no programming experience.
- **You are ready when:** you can use a browser and are willing to predict, run,
  explain, and change small examples. No mathematics prerequisite is assumed.
- **Practice setup:** start with generated Colab notebooks. Unit 1 compares the
  browser and local workflows before later units use projects and command-line tools.
- **Assessment:** lesson checks diagnose understanding; each unit challenge asks
  you to combine its skills in a guided task with assertions and hints.

## What you will be able to do

- trace values, state, decisions, loops, collections, calls, and failures;
- turn a problem statement into examples, small algorithms, and testable functions;
- process Unicode text, files, paths, structured data, and invalid input safely;
- organize a reproducible Git-backed project with a CLI, tests, typing, and CI;
- choose classes, generators, decorators, and context managers based on design needs;
- explain and defend program behavior with tests, logs, and debugging evidence.

## Learning sequence

Python Foundations curriculum version 5 contains **24 units** and **62 cohesive
lessons**. Each unit begins with an Overview and ends with a guided challenge.

| Unit | Focus | Outcome | Apply it |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Learning Workflow and Tools](units/learning-workflow-tools/index.qmd) | Choose a dependable practice environment and use prediction, clean reruns, and evidence to learn deliberately. | [Challenge](units/learning-workflow-tools/challenge.qmd) |
| 2 | [Values, Names, and Numeric Computation](units/numeric-foundations/index.qmd) | Represent quantities, trace assignments, choose numeric operations, and explain rounding decisions. | [Challenge](units/numeric-foundations/challenge.qmd) |
| 3 | [Text, Unicode, Input, and Output](units/text-input-output/index.qmd) | Create, transform, validate, encode, and display text without confusing strings with numbers or bytes. | [Challenge](units/text-input-output/challenge.qmd) |
| 4 | [Boolean Logic and Decisions](units/decisions/index.qmd) | Translate rules into Boolean expressions and branches whose boundary behavior can be traced. | [Challenge](units/decisions/challenge.qmd) |
| 5 | [Loops, Tracing, and State](units/loops-and-state/index.qmd) | Repeat work safely, trace changing state, and prove that a loop makes progress toward stopping. | [Challenge](units/loops-and-state/challenge.qmd) |
| 6 | [Problem Decomposition and Basic Algorithms](units/problem-solving-algorithms/index.qmd) | Turn a written problem into examples, pseudocode, small steps, and a correct search, count, or transformation. | [Challenge](units/problem-solving-algorithms/challenge.qmd) |
| 7 | [Sequences: Lists and Tuples](units/sequences/index.qmd) | Model ordered information, choose mutable or immutable sequences, and use indexing and slicing safely. | [Challenge](units/sequences/challenge.qmd) |
| 8 | [Mappings, Sets, and Nested Data](units/mappings-and-sets/index.qmd) | Choose dictionaries and sets for lookup, uniqueness, counting, and nested records. | [Challenge](units/mappings-and-sets/challenge.qmd) |
| 9 | [Mutability, Identity, and Copying](units/mutability-and-copying/index.qmd) | Predict aliasing and mutation, copy at the intended depth, and avoid accidental shared state. | [Challenge](units/mutability-and-copying/challenge.qmd) |
| 10 | [Functions and Interfaces](units/functions-and-interfaces/index.qmd) | Design focused functions with explicit inputs, return values, contracts, and independent checks. | [Challenge](units/functions-and-interfaces/challenge.qmd) |
| 11 | [Scope, Call Stacks, and Functions as Values](units/scope-and-call-stacks/index.qmd) | Trace names across calls, read stack-shaped execution, and use recursion or function values deliberately. | [Challenge](units/scope-and-call-stacks/challenge.qmd) |
| 12 | [Debugging and Reproducible Failures](units/debugging/index.qmd) | Use tracebacks, controlled experiments, tools, and minimal reproductions to investigate failures from evidence. | [Challenge](units/debugging/challenge.qmd) |
| 13 | [Files, Paths, and Encodings](units/files-and-paths/index.qmd) | Read and write files with explicit paths, encodings, resource lifetimes, and failure expectations. | [Challenge](units/files-and-paths/challenge.qmd) |
| 14 | [Structured Data and Text Patterns](units/structured-data-and-patterns/index.qmd) | Parse structured files and text patterns through a staged, testable validation pipeline. | [Challenge](units/structured-data-and-patterns/challenge.qmd) |
| 15 | [Exceptions and Defensive Programming](units/exceptions-and-validation/index.qmd) | Validate boundaries, raise useful exceptions, and catch only failures the program can handle. | [Challenge](units/exceptions-and-validation/challenge.qmd) |
| 16 | [Modules, Imports, and Standard Library](units/modules-and-standard-library/index.qmd) | Split code across modules, reason about imports, and select standard-library tools before adding dependencies. | [Challenge](units/modules-and-standard-library/challenge.qmd) |
| 17 | [Reproducible Python Projects](units/reproducible-projects/index.qmd) | Arrange source and tests, isolate dependencies, and describe a buildable project with pyproject.toml. | [Challenge](units/reproducible-projects/challenge.qmd) |
| 18 | [Git and Collaboration](units/git-and-collaboration/index.qmd) | Create meaningful commits, work safely with branches and merges, and collaborate through remotes. | [Challenge](units/git-and-collaboration/challenge.qmd) |
| 19 | [Command-Line Applications](units/command-line-applications/index.qmd) | Build commands with explicit arguments, standard streams, exit codes, and testable core behavior. | [Challenge](units/command-line-applications/challenge.qmd) |
| 20 | [Testing with pytest](units/testing-with-pytest/index.qmd) | Turn contracts and boundaries into readable tests, then use failures, fixtures, and parametrization as design feedback. | [Challenge](units/testing-with-pytest/challenge.qmd) |
| 21 | [Documentation, Style, Linting, and Typing](units/maintainable-code/index.qmd) | Improve code safely with documentation, refactoring, formatting, linting, and useful type information. | [Challenge](units/maintainable-code/challenge.qmd) |
| 22 | [Object-Oriented Python and Dataclasses](units/object-oriented-python/index.qmd) | Model cohesive state and behavior with classes and dataclasses while avoiding unnecessary abstraction. | [Challenge](units/object-oriented-python/challenge.qmd) |
| 23 | [Pythonic Iteration and Resource Control](units/pythonic-iteration/index.qmd) | Choose comprehensions, generators, decorators, and context managers when they make intent and lifecycles clearer. | [Challenge](units/pythonic-iteration/challenge.qmd) |
| 24 | [Operating a Reliable Project](units/reliable-project-operations/index.qmd) | Combine configuration, logging, secrets, local quality gates, and CI into an observable project workflow. | [Challenge](units/reliable-project-operations/challenge.qmd) |

## Assessment and progress

Treat each lesson as a lab: predict, run, explain, modify, quiz, and debug. The
unit challenge then asks you to select and combine ideas rather than repeat the
lesson example. Except for the Unit 1 methodology quiz, challenges are designed
for 60–120 minutes and provide a public contract, progressive checks, three
levels of hints, and a debugging-evidence record.

The progress dashboard is private, self-reported browser storage. It does not
submit work, grade artifacts, verify identity, or issue credentials.

::: {.callout-important title="Final project and certificate are coming later"}
A Python Foundations final project and certificate are planned. Requirements,
availability, and participation details will be announced soon.
:::

## Start learning

Begin with the learning method, then move through the sequence in order. Return
to earlier evidence whenever a later task exposes a gap.
